title: The Market for Fake Reviews
eligible_reason: Nov 4 (published article checked): NOT eligible under the main-text rule. The staggered two-bin regressions (first and last Facebook post, product and year-week FE) appear only in Appendix B of the published article (Tables B.1-B.2); the main text reports them in words and its regression table (Table 7) is a single-date matched DiD around the Amazon review purge (ineligible: one adoption date, PSM sample). Not a near miss: no main-text staggered regression. Earlier record (screened from the package and the 2021 MPRA working paper): Tables 10(a) and 11(a) regress weekly product outcomes on binned post indicators with product (id) and year-week (time_week) fixed effects, no controls, no weights, clustered by product. Treatment switches on at product-specific calendar weeks (first Facebook recruitment post; 38 distinct onset weeks among 1,455 focal products with an onset observation) and 2,714 never-recruited comparison products are in the sample. The two post bins ([0,2] and [3+] weeks) make each column a two-bin unstacked event study; the static re-estimation uses post = 1{interval_st >= 0}.
design_notes: Product-week panel (final-dataset-all-products.dta: 314,330 rows, 4,206 products, 43 variables). Focal products (is_focal==1, n=1,492) were observed being promoted in Facebook fake-review groups; interval_st (interval_lt) is the week relative to the first (last) FB post. Non-focal comparison products (n=2,714) have interval_st missing and two_weeks_since = after_two_weeks = 0 throughout, observed over 108 calendar weeks (469-576), overlapping all focal onset weeks (495-549). Table 10(a): post bins relative to first post, sample focal weeks [-8,4] plus all comparison weeks. Table 11(a): post bins relative to last post (onset at interval_lt==1), sample focal weeks [-4,8] plus comparison. Panels (b) interact bins with a coldstart indicator. Section 5 Table 7 / Figure 13 / Tables 12, 14, 15 compare promoted products whose fake reviews survived Amazon's purge with promoted products whose reviews were deleted (after##have_fake_reviews with psmatch2 kernel weights): not eligible. Table 13 (Appendix D) is a continuous-treatment version. R scripts produce descriptive figures only.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 38 distinct first-FB-post calendar weeks (time_week 502-545) among the 1,455 focal products with an interval_st==0 observation; 36 distinct last-post weeks for the Table 11 design. Counted from the data, not from the text.
preferred_spec_note: Headline outcomes inferred from the abstract (ratings, reviews, sales rank); confirm against the article.
published_estimates_note: No article text and no table output files in the package; coefficients must be taken from the published paper or regenerated.

Static equivalent: post = 1{interval_st >= 0}, onset = product-specific first-post week.

specs.treatment_definition: Generated at lines 77-80: two_weeks_since_last = 1 if interval_lt in [1,3]; after_two_weeks_last = 1 if interval_lt > 3, where interval_lt is the week relative to the product's LAST Facebook recruitment post. Treatment here is the end of the fake-review promotion; onset = first full week after the last FB post (interval_lt == 1). Static equivalent: post = 1{interval_lt >= 1}. 36 distinct end-of-promotion calendar weeks.
specs.sample_condition: (interval_lt >= -4 & interval_lt <= 8) | interval_lt == . : focal products within 4 weeks before to 8 weeks after the last FB post (1,491 products) plus all weeks of the 2,714 non-focal comparison products; 259,148 product-weeks
specs.event_bins: [1,3] and [4,8] weeks relative to last FB post
specs.omitted_period: interval_lt in [-4,0] and all comparison-product weeks
specs.notes: FLAG: the switching-on event is the END of the promotion (products stop recruiting fake reviews); formally a staggered binary onset with never-treated comparison products, but the pre-period for treated products is the active-promotion phase. Include or exclude as a judgment call.

specs.sample_condition: as Table 10a
specs.notes: coldstart = product with age<=4 and <=8 cumulative reviews at interval_st==-1 (about 10% of products).

specs.sample_condition: as Table 11a

specs.exclusion_reason: additional staggered regressor (after main effect, i.e., post-first-post indicator for the deleted-reviews control group) and kernel propensity-score weights [pweight=_weight] from psmatch2; comparison group is other promoted products, not never-treated units
specs.treatment_definition: after = 1{interval_st >= 0} (verified: identical to post-first-FB-post in the data); have_fake_reviews = 1 for focal products whose fake reviews were NOT deleted in Amazon's March 2020 purge (1,414 products), 0 for focal products whose reviews were deleted (78 products)
specs.weights: pweight=_weight (psmatch2 kernel, normal, bw 0.005, matched on pre-period avg cumulative reviews, rating, age)
specs.sample_condition: is_focal==1 & interval_st in [-8,4] & matched (_weight != .)
specs.reported_location: Table 7 (Section 5); Figure 13 is the event-study version (line 143: _IweeXhave_* c.after [pweight=_weight])
specs.notes: Tables 12 (alternative purge windows, focal-prod-purge1/2/3.dta), 14 (placebo purge dates, no weights), 15 (NN and LLR matching) are variants of the same design and are likewise ineligible. Table 13 (Appendix D) uses a continuous treatment c.after##c.log_purge_date_diff_abs.

replication/data/focal-prod-purge1.dta, focal-prod-purge2.dta, focal-prod-purge3.dta, focal-prod-fake-before.dta, focal-prod-fake-after.dta (15 MB each; focal products only, alternative purge definitions)

data_files_note: All variables used by Tables 10-11 (avg_rating, log_num_reviews, logrank, log_position, sponsored_dummy, coupon, log_photos_num, verified, log_current_price, two_weeks_since, after_two_weeks, interval_st, interval_lt, id, time_week, is_focal) are present. Product ids are anonymized; README does not describe the data as synthetic or perturbed. Scraped Amazon data.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, estout/esttab, psmatch2, parmby) for all regressions; R for figures only.
priority_note: Eligible, data and code present, variable names verified in the .dta.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Treatment-bin definitions, cohort counts, sample sizes and the meaning of 'after' (= 1{interval_st>=0}) were verified by reading final-dataset-all-products.dta with pandas. Two judgment calls flagged: (i) the two post bins are treated as a binned event study (static version: post = 1{interval_st>=0}); (ii) Table 11(a) specs treat the END of the promotion as the switching-on event and are listed as eligible with a flag. Main-text status of Tables 10-11 inferred from README numbering (Table 13 is explicitly 'Appendix D'); verify when the PDF is available. Published table numbers come from the README (Tables 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15; Figure 13). Note: a project PI (Proserpio) is a coauthor.
hand_check_nov4: Published PDF and web appendix obtained Nov 4; 18 specs moved to data/specs_excluded/ (main-text rule). Team member's own paper (PROTOCOL 6).
